doc.title: Michi Fuji interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: Meeting Junior Mance and playing Harlem Lullaby
summary: At the New School she met Junior Mance; at the first trio try she copied his Harlem Lullaby solo from listening.

venues.name: New School for Jazz and Contemporary Music

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Okay. And that’s where you met Junior [Mance]?
You know we have something in common, that we both like the song “Harlem Lullaby.”
I understand you played that with him the first time you met him? Or is that not quite correct?

The first time, what happened? I was just listening to his “Harlem Lullaby” over and over. And the first time Hide, me and Junior tried it I was really listening, and I played the same place Junior played, Junior had soloed. Junior had soloed. And he saw me. “That’s my solo you just played.” So I learned that the song doesn’t have music so I just listened and played what he played. It’s okay.
